commits.message: [Phase 0] Optimize step loop: numpy rollout + param stack cache + jnp.asarray in PPO
commits.body:
Three per-step performance improvements (no behavioral change):

1. Rollout buffer now uses NumPy arrays instead of JAX. Each step previously
   called buf.at[ptr].set() (creates a new JAX array) for 4 fields × n_agents.
   NumPy in-place assignment is ~20x faster (~1ms vs ~23ms at 45 agents).
   ppo_update calls jnp.asarray() at the start to convert before JAX ops.

2. Stacked policy params cache (_get_stacked_params / _update_param_slot).
   Previously rebuilt jtu.tree_map stack from scratch every step (~51ms).
   Now cached by agent-id tuple; rebuilt only when births/deaths occur.
   After PPO update, only the changed agent's slot is updated via .at[].set().
   Saves ~50ms on the ~99% of steps with no population change.

3. Removed redundant get_observation + policy_forward in PPO trigger.
   The computed last_value was discarded anyway (ppo.py hardcodes last_value=0.0).

Result: 317ms/step → ~116ms/step measured at 45 agents (~8.6 steps/s in
isolated benchmark); 4.4 steps/s measured in full loop at 87 agents (step 5000).
25k smoke test projected ~1.5-2h vs original ~6h estimate.

- tests/test_checkpoint_jax.py: 9 tests covering roundtrip, atomic

commits.body:

--xla_cpu_enable_fast_math and --xla_cpu_use_thunk_runtime. Flags are

  Before: 7.0 steps/s (pre-PPO, 500 steps, --runtime mac.yaml)
  After:  9.8 steps/s (same run)

and stds) are identical at the displayed precision — fast-math's
sub-ULP numerical differences don't affect anything we care about
at the scale of this workload.

commits.body:

to determine where real time goes when sim_step_core runs slow.

Key finding from running this on Mac at 198 agents (M4 Pro, fast-math):
  physics (phyjax2d)        72.3% of step time
  energy + births + food    19.5%
  observations               7.2%
  eating (O(N^2) catch)      0.5%  ← was suspected bottleneck; isn't
  policy sample              0.5%

commits.message: [Perf] Batch the per-step PPO readiness check (29% Mac speedup)
commits.body:
Previously the runner called np.array(sim_state.rollout_ptrs) every
step, which blocks the Python loop waiting for GPU/CPU to finish
sim_step_core. Now we only check readiness every PPO_CHECK_EVERY steps
(default 10, overridable via EVO_PPO_CHECK_EVERY env var).

Measured on Mac M4 Pro (fast-math enabled), 2000 steps, seed 0,
--runtime mac.yaml:

  K=1  (old behavior): 2.1 steps/s
  K=10 (new default):  2.7 steps/s     ~29% faster

On L4 GPU the sync cost is larger, so the win is likely ≥ 29%. Have
not re-benchmarked on GPU (that's $0.70/hr) but will observe the rate
on the real Phase 1a run.

Correctness tradeoff: when an agent's rollout fills (ptrs hits
rollout_steps=1024), subsequent sim_step_core calls clip the write
index to slot 1023 (src/jax_sim.py:123) — so the final slot may be
overwritten by up to (PPO_CHECK_EVERY - 1) later observations before
PPO fires. At K=10 and rollout_steps=1024 that's 0.1% of the rollout
being 1-9 steps "late" per update.

Empirically at step 2000, K=1 vs K=10 gives:
  prey=244 vs 243, pred=23 vs 24 (within normal stochastic variance)
  w_pred mean: -0.04 vs -0.05 (both show fear direction)
  w_prey mean: +0.00 vs +0.00 (identical at 2-decimal precision)

Well within seed-to-seed variance. Set EVO_PPO_CHECK_EVERY=1 to
recover exact-timing baseline for comparison runs.

Final-flush safety: _maybe_fire_ppo is also called before each
checkpoint write and once more at the end of the run, so saved state
always reflects a post-PPO-sweep view (no stale in-progress
rollouts).

All 141 tests still pass (tests call sim_step_core directly and
are unaffected by the runner-side batching).

commits.message: [Infra] spot_orchestrator: auto-create NAT + SSH retry with backoff
commits.body:
Two reliability fixes after the first run failed on us-west1-a:

1. Each region needs its own Cloud NAT (NAT is regional). The
   orchestrator now calls ensure_nat(zone) right after a successful
   VM create, checking for the router/NAT in the VM's region and
   creating them if missing. Idempotent — no-ops when they exist.

2. Fresh VMs aren't ready for SSH for ~30-90s after create (ssh key
   propagation, sshd startup). wait_for_ssh() polls with backoff
   (30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180s — up to ~7 min of patience) before
   handing off to provision().

No behavior change when things work; just way more tolerant of the
normal transient failures of GCP spot capacity handoff.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] Preemption-hardened orchestrator via GCP startup-script
commits.body:
Previous orchestrator installed apt packages + jax[cuda12] via SSH
from the laptop. That took 10-15 minutes during which the spot VM
was especially vulnerable to preemption, and mid-install preemption
killed SSH and the orchestrator exited.

New architecture:

- scripts/vm_startup.sh: idempotent bootstrap script passed as
  instance metadata. Runs as root on every VM boot (including after
  spot preemption + restart). Installs apt packages, creates venv,
  installs jax[cuda12]. If repo + phase1a_loop.sh have been uploaded,
  also installs requirements and starts the tmux training session.
  Logs to /var/log/evo-startup.log. Writes /tmp/evo-ready once the
  base env is ready.

- scripts/spot_orchestrator.py rewritten as a reconcile-loop:
  1. Get (or poll for) a zone with spot capacity; create VM with
     vm_startup.sh as startup-script metadata.
  2. Each cycle, describe the VM and drive it to the target state:
     TERMINATED -> start; RUNNING -> wait for ready marker; then
     upload repo + loop script if missing; then start tmux if missing.
  3. Every step is idempotent and failure-tolerant. No step ever
     calls sys.exit — failures just leave the cycle incomplete and
     the next iteration retries.
  4. On preemption restart, vm_startup.sh restarts the tmux session
     automatically; the orchestrator just has to notice RUNNING.

Wait windows:
  * wait_for_ssh: up to 6 min for sshd + key propagation
  * wait_for_ready_marker: up to 30 min for jax[cuda12] install to
    finish on first boot (it's ~500MB of CUDA wheels)

State is still in .claude-orch-state.json so rerunning picks up the
existing VM.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] spot_orchestrator: detect preemption mid-wait, faster reconcile
commits.body:
Two fixes after observing the orchestrator stuck in a 30-min wait
loop while the VM was already TERMINATED:

1. wait_for_ready_marker polls VM status each iteration and returns
   False immediately if status != RUNNING. The outer reconcile loop
   then restarts the VM on the next cycle.

2. READY_MARKER_ATTEMPTS dropped from 60 (30 min) to 10 (5 min).
   Longer install progress naturally spans multiple reconcile cycles
   since the startup-script is idempotent — no reason to hold one
   cycle open for 30 min while pretending nothing is wrong.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] GCS-backed checkpoints + persistent-stockout fallback
commits.body:
Two fixes that together make the spot orchestrator survive sustained
GCP capacity pressure:

1. GCS-backed checkpoints (cross-zone recovery).
   vm_startup.sh now reads instance-metadata key `gcs-bucket` and:
     - on boot, `gsutil rsync` from gs://$BUCKET/results -> local
       (restores a new VM to the last saved state of the previous VM)
     - starts a tmux session that pushes local results -> GCS every
       5 min (incremental, survives preemption)
   The orchestrator creates the bucket on startup, attaches it via
   metadata to each VM, and gives the VM cloud-platform scope so its
   default service account can read/write.

2. Persistent-stockout fallback (delete+recreate elsewhere).
   After 3 consecutive stockout failures on `instances start` in the
   same zone (~15 min), the orchestrator deletes the stuck VM and
   polls all zones for fresh capacity. With GCS-backed checkpoints
   in place, the new VM pulls prior results before resuming training —
   minimal progress loss.

This unblocks the case we just hit: us-central1-a preempted our VM
and then refused to restart it due to stockout. Before these fixes
the orchestrator would loop forever on same-zone retry. After these
fixes, new VM in an available zone with checkpoints restored.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] spot_orchestrator: --on-demand flag instead of auto-fallback
commits.body:
The decision of when to abandon spot is a user judgment, not an
orchestrator policy. Replaced the time-based auto-fallback with an
explicit --on-demand flag.

Usage: when spot capacity is chronically bad and you'd rather pay
the premium for certainty, kill the spot orchestrator and re-run:

    python3 scripts/spot_orchestrator.py --on-demand --seed 0

Everything else stays identical — same state file, same GCS
checkpoint bucket, same reconcile loop. The new VM just skips the
--provisioning-model=SPOT / termination-action flags, so it's a
regular on-demand VM that won't be preempted.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] Line-buffer runner stdout so phase1a.log updates in real time
commits.body:
Without unbuffered output, Python's stdout piped through tee sat in
a ~4KB block buffer. On a real Phase 1a run the first log line at
step 5000 emits about 150 bytes, so nothing appeared in phase1a.log
for many minutes while training was quietly running on the GPU. Made
it look like training was hung when it was actually fine.

Fix: wrap the runner with stdbuf -oL -eL python -u, and pipe through
stdbuf -oL tee, forcing line-buffering end to end. Progress lines now
appear in phase1a.log within seconds of being printed.

Only the orchestrator-generated phase1a_loop.sh script was changed;
tests and repo code are untouched.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Tools] status.py monitoring dashboard + docs/monitoring.md
commits.body:
Goal: day-to-day operations of the GCP Phase 1a run should never
require remembering raw gcloud commands or manually tailing logs.

- scripts/status.py: one-shot status CLI. Reads the orchestrator

  the last lines of phase1a.log, parses the latest progress line
  (Step N/M | prey=... | w_pred=... | ...), and renders a compact
  color-coded dashboard: VM status, provisioning model, training
  progress, ETA, GPU utilization, population counts, reward-weight
  means (with green indicators when fear + affiliation are
  emerging in the right direction), retry count, and the
  canonical tail-log / tmux-attach commands footer. --follow N
  refreshes in place every N seconds.

- tests/test_status.py: 10 unit tests for the log-line regex + the
  format helpers. Pure-function coverage; subprocess / gcloud paths
  are validated live.

- docs/monitoring.md: tools at a glance, quick-reference one-liners,
  status dashboard walkthrough, lifecycle operations (start /
  resume / on-demand switch / teardown), and a troubleshooting
  section with the failure modes we hit during this session.

- README.md: link to the new monitoring doc alongside gcp-setup
  and gcp-spot.

Full test suite: 161 passed + 3 skipped (was 151 + 3).

commits.message: [Config] Shorten spot checkpoint interval: 25k -> 10k steps
commits.body:
Four spot VM attempts today lost 100% of training progress because
every preemption happened before the first checkpoint was written.
Checkpoint interval was 25k steps (~12 min at 34 sps), but measured
preemption window during contested capacity is ~10-15 min. Shortening
to 10k (~5 min wall clock) lets us survive typical preemptions —
several checkpoints land before the VM is reclaimed, so new VMs
resume from GCS instead of starting from step 0.

Save overhead goes from ~3% to ~5-7% of wall clock, which is still
much cheaper than the total-progress-loss we'd been eating.

If spot capacity remains chronically bad, on-demand (via
--on-demand on spot_orchestrator.py) stays a clean off-ramp.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] orchestrator: surface actual gcloud error instead of assuming stockout
commits.body:
Prior behavior: any failed `gcloud compute instances create` was logged
as "trying <zone>..." with no follow-up, so quota errors, permission
problems, and all other non-capacity failures were invisibly rolled
up as "stockout, sleeping 10min".

Hit this today when 200GB orphan disks pushed us past SSD_TOTAL_GB
quota in us-central1 — orchestrator reported "all zones stockout"
but the real error was quota, fixable in seconds by deleting the
stuck disk.

Now each failed create logs a one-line summary (stockout, SSD quota,
general quota, permissions, already-exists, or the last line of
gcloud's error).
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] orchestrator: start gcs-sync sidecar directly, not via startup-script
commits.body:
vm_startup.sh only launched the gcs-sync tmux session if the repo was
already on disk when it ran. But the orchestrator uploads the repo
AFTER the startup-script has finished its first pass — so gcs-sync
was never launched on a fresh VM, which meant local checkpoints
never synced to GCS. Local disk is durable for on-demand VMs, but
we lose our cross-zone safety net for spot, and there's no backup
against accidental VM deletion for either mode.

Fix: start both phase1a AND gcs-sync tmux sessions from the
orchestrator's start_tmux() step, which runs after the repo is
guaranteed to be in place. Idempotent — if gcs-sync is already
running, it's left alone.

Also reported in the orchestrator log output now, so a missing
gcs-sync is immediately visible.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Docs] Add K&D 2024/2025 arXiv .tex sources for LLM-readable reference
commits.body:
LLM agents can now grep the actual paper text directly instead of

commits.message: [Tools] status.py: hardcode project/account + retry on TERMINATED
commits.body:
Two fixes after status.py returned wildly wrong data (reported a VM
as TERMINATED in spot mode when it was actually RUNNING on-demand):

1. Pin CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT and CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT as env vars
   for every gcloud subprocess call. If the user's shell-global
   gcloud config points at a different project (as likely happened
   since they maintain another project for unrelated work), we were
   querying the wrong thing and silently getting back a same-named
   VM from that project. Now status.py is safe to run from any
   terminal without sourcing scripts/gcloud-env.sh first.

2. Retry once with a 2s delay if describe returns TERMINATED. GCP
   describe is eventually-consistent and very occasionally returns
   stale state. A single retry smooths over transient blips; a
   genuinely TERMINATED VM stays TERMINATED on the second call so
   real outages still surface.

Usage unchanged:
  python3 scripts/status.py
  python3 scripts/status.py --follow 30

All 10 tests still pass.

commits.message: [Docs] Record April 2026 spot experience + on-demand as the default
commits.body:
After a multi-hour attempt to run Phase 1a seed 0 on GCP spot L4
VMs that kept getting preempted within 10-15 min of creation (before
any checkpoint could land in GCS), we fell back to on-demand. This
commit captures the lessons so future runs start with the right
expectations.

- docs/gcp-spot.md: new "⚠ When spot works — and when it doesn't"
  admonition at the top, plus an updated caveat to the cost table
  noting that contested-capacity runs can cost more than on-demand
  if every attempt ends in preemption without forward progress.

- docs/monitoring.md: expanded troubleshooting with two new
  sections — "SSD quota exceeded" (the error the orchestrator used
  to mask as stockout, fixed in a previous commit; now this is the
  user-facing playbook when it happens) and "Telling if spot isn't
  going to work" (concrete decision signals + the one-liner to
  switch modes). GCS-backed checkpoints from prior spot attempts
  carry over, so the switch is non-destructive.

- README.md: note on the gcp-spot link that on-demand is the default
  recommendation; try spot only when capacity is healthy.

No code changes — the spot path stays intact as a one-flag option
for future runs when the GCP L4 market is less contested.

commits.message: [Docs+Validation] Apply K&D audit corrections across docs and gate criteria
commits.body:

and one real bug in the Phase 1a gate criteria. Sim code is unchanged.

commits.message: [Dashboard+Docs] Align K&D expectations with paper §4.2 medium-mouth bimodality
commits.body:
Reading docs/papers/sources/kd-2025/main.tex §4.2 (default condition =
medium mouth + Δn=0.5) revealed our success criteria + dashboard
coloring over-simplify the paper's actual findings.

Docs (technical-spec §14):
- Split criteria into Core / Predator-side / Environmental, matching the
  paper's structure.
- Criterion 1 (prey w_pred) now explicitly notes the bimodality K&D
  describe: seeds 2 & 4 ("P2 lineage") evolve counter-intuitively
  positive w_pred, expected to correlate with strongly positive w_prey.
  Our 3/5 threshold still works; just documenting the "why."
- Criterion 3 split into 3 (prey w_eat universal >0) and 4 (prey w_act
  consistently >0, which the old spec didn't mention at all).
- Added criterion 5 (predator w_eat >0 in 3/5 medium mouth — noting the
  paper's mouth-size sensitivity per §4.3).
- Added criterion 6 (predator w_pred "almost positively" — the social
  following finding we weren't gating on).
- Added criterion 7 (predator w_prey >0 most seeds, with the coupling
  to prey w_pred K&D describe).
- Added criterion 9 (steady-state population near K&D Table 1 defaults
  ~349 prey / ~23 pred — catches cap-pinning bugs).
- Noted predator w_act is explicitly bimodal; don't gate on sign.

Dashboard (GcpMonitor.tsx TrainingCard):
- prey.w_pred color-coding changed from wantSign="-" to null because
  K&D expect bimodal, not unilaterally negative. Note now explains
  both outcomes.
- prey.w_act now wantSign="+" (it should be positive, was shown as
  informational-only).
- pred.w_eat note softened to "medium mouth" so the color expectation
  is scoped; wantSign="+" retained for our condition.
- pred.w_prey note mentions the coupling to prey.w_pred.
- Added an amber "at cap" callout when population hits prey_cap=450
  or predator_cap=50, pointing at K&D steady-state for comparison.

No code-logic changes; purely documentation + UI copy.

commits.message: [Dashboard] Remove Card overflow-hidden so tooltips can escape the border
commits.body:
Tooltips positioned above rows near the top of a card were being
clipped by the Card's outer overflow-hidden — not a z-index problem,
which only affects stacking order, but an overflow-container problem
that clips any descendant visually exceeding the bounds.

The overflow-hidden wasn't earning its keep: no child has a background
that would bleed past the rounded corners (only the outer div has a
background; header/body/footer are padding + border separators).

Removing it lets Tooltip's absolute-positioned popover render freely
outside the card. z-30 still stacks it above sibling cards correctly.

Progress bar keeps its own overflow-hidden — needed to clip the fill
to its rounded container.

commits.message: [Replay] Scrubbable 2D canvas replays + GCS pipeline
commits.body:
New /replay page in the dashboard plays back per-step predator/prey
trajectories on a Canvas 2D renderer. Source is pluggable via
VITE_REPLAYS_BASE_URL: same-origin /replays/ for committed files, or a
public GCS bucket for hands-off production use — no dashboard backend.

Pipeline:
  scripts/replay_recorder.py  — in-line ring buffer hooks into the
    training loop, captures only inside the window leading up to each
    flush boundary (zero cost outside). Quantizes positions to uint16
    (~0.015-unit precision in a 960-unit world) and energy to uint8,
    shrinking files ~3x.
  scripts/replay_upload.py    — upload, list, delete, index rebuild on
    gs://evo-reward-replays-public/.
  scripts/replay_retention.py — three retention policies (last_n,
    milestones, logarithmic) with a pluggable registry. Applied after
    each upload; evicted replays are deleted from GCS.
  scripts/replay.py           — CLI: list, fetch, render, all, clean,
    list-remote, prune (with --dry-run), delete.
  scripts/replay_render.py    — simulated re-sim from a saved checkpoint
    for watching runs that predate the in-line recorder.
  scripts/setup_replays_bucket.sh — one-time gcloud commands to create
    the public-read + CORS-enabled bucket.

scripts/run_experiment_jax.py calls recorder.step(state, step+1) each
tick; boundary check uses the Python loop variable so recording adds
zero host sync outside the window.

The React loader (replayLoader.ts) eagerly dequantizes uint16/uint8
sections into Float32Array so the canvas renderer stays dtype-agnostic;
falls back to zero-copy views for legacy float32 replays.
commits.author: Axel Browne
